text:
lina: Quick FYI: my team's sample app started failing pyright on CI after we bumped the autogen models. error message complains about TypedDict vs BaseModel usage. anyone seen this mismatch?

rahul: hmm, do you mean generated models are using TypedDicts in one template and pydantic BaseModel in another?

lina: yes. our server-side sample (sync) uses pydantic, async sample app uses TypedDicts in the response types. pyright flags e.g. `Incompatible types in assignment (expression has type 'CompletionResponse', variable has type 'CompletionResponseTypedDict')`.

zach: that's surprising. codegen used to pick pydantic for everything. maybe a recent perf branch switched to TypedDicts for lighter-weight runtime.

lina: sample snippet: ```py
# gen_async_types.py (autogen)
from typing import TypedDict, List, Optional
class ChoiceTD(TypedDict):
    text: str

class CompletionResponseTD(TypedDict, total=False):
    choices: Optional[List[ChoiceTD]]

# usage in async sample app
async def greet():
    resp: CompletionResponseTD = await client.generate("hello")
    print(resp["choices"])
```

rahul: pyright treats TypedDict as structural; pydantic BaseModel is nominal and returns model instances. mixing them causes the typechecker to see different shapes. runtime might still work if models export dicts but static types differ.

zach: another wrinkle: our async client has a `return_model=BaseModel` flag in some call paths but codegen for samples assumed dict output and annotated the stubs as TypedDict. mismatch introduced by sample-templates change.

lina: hitting this in strict-checker mode only, but we want CI to be green for users who have strict settings.

rahul: proposal: unify sample templates to prefer pydantic BaseModel types for exported SDK types (consistency), and provide a lightweight shim in samples that does `.dict()` when the user wants raw dicts. also add a note to onboarding about pyright caveats.

zach: agree. small backwards-compat note: some users prefer TypedDicts to avoid pydantic overhead. maybe opt-in generator flag --use-typedict. default should be BaseModel for parity.

lina: also saw a pyright-specific suppression in an unrelated repo: `# type: ignore[reportIncompatibleVariable]` — not ideal to suggest but might be a short-term workaround.

dev-bot: opened issue #1347 in sdk-gen repo: "generator: default to BaseModel for SDK sample types; opt-in TypedDict". Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-gen/issues/1347

rahul: I'll pick up the generator change. plan: change templates, add test that compares sync vs async emitted stubs, and run pyright against sample app in CI.

zach: I'll add a small integration test that runs the sample app with strict pyright config so we catch regressions.

ci-bot: ci/pipeline #4710 queued: add pyright strict check for samples.

lina: thanks team — once generator PR lands I'll re-run my project tests and report if anything else is broken. :thumbsup:
